text: For about four months I had panic attacks almost every day, especially in crowds or when there was loud music. I couldn't go to concerts anymore, which had been my favourite thing. I also had derealisation, everything looked like a film set, flat and fake, and I would sometimes touch walls to make sure they were real. I had flashbacks to the loop, especially when I was tired. Sometimes I would look at a clock and get scared that time would stop again. I dropped one of my courses at uni because I couldn't concentrate.
Ein paar Wochen lang hatte ich Angst vor Herzrasen und habe ständig meinen Puls gemessen. Danach ging es wieder.

Persistent depersonalisation and derealisation for almost two years. I would look in the mirror and not recognise myself, or I'd see myself but feel nothing, like looking at a stranger. The world felt like a thin layer over the void I saw in the ceremony. I couldn't shake the belief that reality is fundamentally empty and hostile.

I developed severe depression within a few months. I lost interest in everything. I quit my job as a graphic designer because I couldn't see the point in making things pretty when underneath it's all nothing. I had suicidal thoughts for a long period, not because I wanted to die exactly, but because I felt like I was already dead and nothing mattered.

Insomnia was terrible. I was afraid to fall asleep because the moment between waking and sleeping felt like sliding back into the black space. I'd sleep 3-4 hours a night for months. I also had intrusive images of the entity, its face (it didn't really have a face but I see it as one now), especially in the dark. I couldn't be in a dark room for a long time and slept with the lights on.

Physically I had chest tightness and a sort of buzzing in my body. Also tinnitus that started after the retreat and never fully went away. My relationship with my partner fell apart because I was so absent.
Anxiety for about a week, then fine

Seit der Erfahrung sehe ich Visual Snow, vor allem auf hellen Flächen und im Dunkeln. Außerdem habe ich Nachbilder und manchmal Lichtschlieren, wenn sich etwas bewegt. Das macht mir große Angst, weil ich befürchte, dass es nie wieder weggeht. In den ersten Monaten hatte ich dazu noch Depersonalisation und das Gefühl, nicht richtig in meinem Körper zu sein.
Recurring intrusive thoughts that reality is fake and that the beings are watching. Strong fear of death that I never had before. Couldn't smoke weed anymore without panicking.

The weeks after were the worst of my life. I had constant derealisation, the world looked like a screen, and depersonalisation, I didn't feel like I was inside my body. I had panic attacks several times a day, often triggered by nothing. I couldn't work for two months. I also became quite depressed because I thought I had broken my brain.
Slowly it improved, mostly over the first six months. Now, two years later, I only get mild DR when I'm very tired or stressed. Looking back I think the experience also showed me how much I'd been trying to control everything in my life, and losing control so completely forced me to face that. I'm more humble now.
Ich hatte danach lange Zeit Angst vor anderen Menschen und war misstrauisch, auch gegenüber engen Freunden.

After the hospital stay I was diagnosed with substance-induced psychotic disorder and put on antipsychotics. The psychotic symptoms faded over about two months, but what came after was in some ways worse.

First, a very deep depression. The antipsychotics made me feel flat and slow, and on top of that I was ashamed and terrified. I had to defer my final year at university. I moved back in with my parents. I spent most days in bed. I had thoughts that I had ruined my life and that I would never be able to trust my own mind again.

Second, a constant fear that the psychosis would come back. Any unusual thought, any coincidence, any song that seemed meaningful would send me into a panic, checking whether I was 'going crazy again'. I would ask my mum several times a day if I seemed normal. I couldn't watch films with conspiracy themes or anything about the end of the world.

Third, I had what I later learned is HPPD: visual snow, trails behind moving objects, and the patterns on surfaces sometimes moving slightly. Not as strong as on LSD but constant. That made it much harder to believe I was recovering, because I could literally see that something was still different.

Fourth, intrusive memories of the hospital, especially the moment I was strapped to a bed in the ER. I'd have flashbacks to that out of nowhere, and I'd get very upset when I saw ambulances or heard sirens. I had nightmares about being trapped in the bathtub, with the water running and running.

I also lost a lot of friends during this time, partly because I withdrew and partly because they didn't know how to deal with what happened. My concentration was terrible for over a year. Reading a page of a book was hard.

It took about two years before I felt somewhat like myself again. I went back and finished my degree. The visual snow is still there but I've mostly made peace with it. I still get anxious when I notice 'meaningful' coincidences and have to remind myself that they're just coincidences.

Monatelang hatte ich eine tiefe Existenzangst. Ich hatte das Gefühl, dass nichts einen Sinn hat und dass ich jederzeit einfach verschwinden könnte. Ich war depressiv, habe mich zurückgezogen und konnte mich über nichts freuen. Mit der Zeit habe ich aber auch gemerkt, dass mich die Erfahrung dazu gebracht hat, mich mit wichtigen Fragen zu beschäftigen, die ich vorher verdrängt hatte. Heute sehe ich vieles klarer.
Monatelang Panikattacken, vor allem nachts. Ich hatte ständig Angst, dass mein Herz stehen bleibt, und war mehrmals in der Notaufnahme, aber es war immer alles in Ordnung.
